# Tresor: performance / UX smoothness pass

Date: 2026-10-04. Builds: baseline = commit d34d5d8 (production build). Final = this change (production build).

**Every number below was measured. Nothing is estimated.** The tables at the end are generated by `tests/perf/report.py` from the JSON files in this folder.

## How it was measured

- **Harness:** Chrome (headless, real compositor) driven by Playwright + CDP (`tests/perf/profile.py`). It runs a real scroll gesture (`Input.synthesizeScrollGesture`: wheel ticks on desktop, touch-emulated on phones) over up to 12,000 px.
- **What it records during the scroll only:**
  - every rAF timestamp, giving frame intervals, dropped frames (> 1.5x the vsync interval) and p95 frame time
  - Long Animation Frames with script attribution, and long tasks
  - React commits (a minimal DevTools hook)
  - CDP script / style / layout time and counts, plus heap
  - running animations, playing videos, image over-decode and CLS
- **Traced pass:** one extra run per page and width sums paint, raster, layerize and decode.
- **Pages and widths:** home, menu, product (cake and pastry), Our Story, Cake Playground, cart, checkout and admin, at 1440 / 1280 / 1024 / 430 / 390.
- **Devices:** phones run at 4x CPU throttle and DPR 3. Desktop runs at 2x throttle and DPR 1, because this machine is a fast 8-core and showed zero dropped frames at 1x, which can't discriminate.
- **Repetitions:** 2–3 reps, taking the median run.
- **Stages:** A current, B Lenis forced off, C scroll-linked work re-engineered, D paint/media, E final.
- **Interleaved headline run:** it measures the baseline build (:3005) and the final build (:3004) back to back (`tests/perf/paired.py`). This was needed because the machine is shared. One isolated E run happened during an unrelated load spike and showed home at 22 fps; that build measured 60 fps both before and after the spike. Those rows were re-measured, and the headline uses the interleaved run.
- **Attribution:** `tests/perf/attribute.py` (CPU profile by chunk/function, running animations, paint by DOM node).
- **Visual regression:** `tests/perf/visual_diff.py`, a pixel diff of the same scroll positions across both builds.

## Bottlenecks found (in order of measured cost)

1. **Per-hook scroll measuring (the largest script cost while scrolling).**
   - Framer's `useScroll({ target })` re-measures its target on every scroll frame, once per hook: an offsetParent walk plus clientWidth/clientHeight reads.
   - The story page has about 15 of these hooks (ScrollScene, Parallax per collage tile, years, finale, team portrait); home has about 10.
   - CPU profile, story at 390: 835 ms busy during one scroll, most of it in the scroll-info chunk.
2. **Cake Playground re-rendering on every animation frame.**
   - `AnimatedNumber` called setState on every frame of its count-up, about 27 re-renders of the whole studio per price change.
   - 8 option clicks produced 135–164 React commits.
3. **Decorative loops that never stop.**
   - Every Our Story film and the Customer Love section ran an infinite grain animation with `mix-blend-mode: overlay`, including off-screen.
   - At the bottom of the story page, 6 off-screen grains were still animating.
   - Each grain layer was 4x the area of its film (`inset: -50%`).
   - The hero scroll cue and the empty-bag icon were Framer JS keyframe loops, running on the main thread every frame forever. The cue's `originY` animation can't be composited.
4. **Layout shift in the story craft scene.**
   - The craft line swaps between sentences of different lengths, so the column resized and the frame jumped.
   - CLS 0.03 on phones (sources: `craft-frame`, `craft-copy`).

Investigated and **not** a bottleneck (left alone):
- **Lenis:** see below.
- **Scroll-driven React state:** `useMotionValueEvent(... setActive)` already fires only on threshold changes, with 2–8 commits per full-page scroll.
- **StoreProvider:** no commits while scrolling; localStorage writes happen only on change.
- **Image over-decode:** median decoded/displayed ratio 0.66.
- **Video:** already `preload="none"` (except the eager opening film), plays only near the viewport, and was paused at the end of every run.
- **Click handlers:** 18–43 ms at 4x throttle.

## Lenis decision (measured)

- **Cost:** Lenis adds script time (home 533 vs 412 ms per scroll; story 752 vs 680 ms). Most of it is its per-frame `window.scrollTo`.
- **Smoothness:** native scrolling was not smoother. Dropped frames: home 0.0% with Lenis vs 1.02% without; story 0.0% vs 1.19%; the cake product page went the other way, 0.98% vs 0.0%. All differences were within about 1%.
- **Idle:** its always-on rAF loop costs about 4 ms of script per 4 s idle.
- **Verdict:** Lenis stays, unchanged (DEC-014).

## Changes

| Change | Why (measurement) | Where |
|---|---|---|
| One scroll source: a shared scrollY motion value and one passive listener. Element positions are measured on mount/resize only, and per-frame progress is arithmetic. Offsets keep Framer's semantics. | Bottleneck 1 | `components/scroll-progress.ts`, `cinematic.tsx` (ScrollScene, HorizontalTrack, Parallax), `cake.tsx`, `story/chapters.tsx`, `story/finale.tsx`, `story/team-chapter.tsx` |
| `AnimatedNumber` writes in-between numbers to its own text node. React renders only the final value. | Bottleneck 2 | `components/motion.tsx` |
| Grain only animates while its film/section is near the viewport (`.is-live`, toggled by the film's existing IntersectionObserver, with no re-render). The layer shrank from `inset -50%` to `-8%` (about 3x less blended area), and keyframes were rescaled so the jitter moves the same distance. | Bottleneck 3 | `story/primitives.tsx` (`useLiveWhileVisible`), `story/customer-love.tsx`, `globals.css` |
| Scroll cue and empty-bag bob became CSS transform keyframes with the same curve (cubic-bezier .42,0,.58,1) and duration. The cue's origin flip is expressed as translate + scale. Still off under reduced motion. | Bottleneck 3 | `home-scenes.tsx`, `cart/page.tsx`, `globals.css` |
| The craft line reserves the tallest line's height (invisible stacked copies). | Bottleneck 4 | `story/chapters.tsx`, `globals.css` |

Also fixed during the stress-test triage: the Cake Playground draft autosave (debounced 400 ms) now flushes on pagehide, tab hide and unmount, so the last edit before leaving is never lost.

## Before → after (interleaved run; full tables below)

- **Main-thread script during one scroll:**
  - home 482 → 242 ms (1440), 479 → 245 (1024), 604 → 233 (390)
  - story 730 → 326, 706 → 303, 962 → 383
  - cake product 86 → 74 / 126 → 107
  - menu 51 → 46 / 78 → 71 (control page: no scroll scenes)
- **Cake Playground React commits for 8 option clicks:** 135–155 → 10–11. Main-thread time for 6 clicks on a throttled phone: 485 → 338 ms.
- **Dropped frames:**
  - story at 390: 1.8% → 0.45%
  - home at 390: 0.22% → 0.0%
  - all other pages 0–1.1% both before and after, which is within run-to-run noise (about ±1%)
  - p95 frame time is the same before and after (18.1 ms at this machine's 56.7 Hz cadence during the run)
- **Running animations at peak during a story scroll:** 16–18 → 11–12. At the end of the page: 8 → 2.
- **Idle (4 s, mid-page):**
  - home script 44 → 6 ms (1440), 94 → 22 ms (390)
  - story style 48 → 24 ms (1440), 113 → 51 ms (390)
  - story running animations 7 → 2
- **Reduced motion:**
  - home script 324 → 138 (1440) and 550 → 231 (390); story 506 → 156 and 842 → 294
  - dropped frames unchanged, at 0–0.54%
  - the old per-hook measuring ran even when reduced motion disabled the motion
- **CLS during a full story scroll (layout-shift observer, separate probe):** at 390, 2 shifts / 0.028 → 0 shifts; at 1440, 2 shifts / 0.008 → 0 shifts.

What this means: on this machine both builds already hold the display's cadence, so the visible frame rate barely moves. What changed is headroom. The main thread does roughly half the work while scrolling (60% less on the story page), which is what keeps slower phones and laptops on cadence. No "60 fps" claim is made.

## Visual regression

- **Animated:** 102 frames compared (home, story and cake product at 14 scroll positions; menu, Cake Playground and cart at 3; each at 1440 and 390). 94 are pixel-identical.
- **Cart:** the 0.02–0.14% differences are antialiasing of the bag icon, from the CSS bob instead of the JS bob.
- **Craft scene (DEC-016), the only real difference:**
  - story-1440 at 22–30% of the page (2.3% / 1.5% of pixels)
  - story-390 at 15–22% (16% / 28%)
  - while a short line shows, the block sits about 15 px higher on desktop and about 30 px higher on phones (the whole stage)
  - side-by-side images are in `.tresor/test-results/screenshots/perf-visual/` (git-ignored)
- **Reduced motion:** 84 / 84 frames are identical.

## Remaining (measured, not fixed)

- **Story page on phones, layerize ~450–900 ms and paint ~300–470 ms per traced scroll.** Many composited layers (collage tiles, films, reveals). The document layer repaints about 365 times per scroll at about 0.3–1 ms each. A promotion experiment (`will-change` on every transformed element) cut that by only about 12%, so it was not shipped.
- **Our Story "8+" numeral (`background-clip: text` with a scroll-linked background-position) and the finale wordmark fill.** These repaint their text every frame by design; changing that would change the effect.
- **Lenis's per-frame `window.scrollTo`.** It is inherent to Lenis, and Lenis was kept on measured smoothness.
- **Cake Playground click latency: 40–160 ms to next paint at 4x throttle,** within the INP "good" threshold. It is mostly Framer layout projection for the sliding selection indicators (part of the design).
- **Media pipeline (AVIF/WebP, srcSet).** All current imagery is git-ignored placeholder material that never ships. Production shows the tone gradients. The `Media` component already does lazy/eager, `decoding=async`, `fetchpriority` and mobile crops, so the AVIF/srcSet pipeline belongs with the real photography.
- **Not measurable in this harness:** GPU cost of the header's `backdrop-filter: blur(18px)` and of mix-blend layers on real phone GPUs. Check on a device.
- **Single-run noise:** two final-build runs show one long animation frame each (home 1440: 52 ms; story 390: 84 ms) where the baseline run had none. Other reps of the same build show none.
